newsitem.title: FINLAND: SANTASALO SEES '97 EPS UP DESPITE ISSUES.
newsitem.headline: SANTASALO SEES '97 EPS UP DESPITE ISSUES.

text.p: Engineering group Santasalo-JOT Oy CEO Heikki Lehtonen said on Thursday group 1997 earnings per share would beat 1996 EPS due to an acquisition although it would issue one million new shares to finance the deal.
Santasalo said earlier it would buy plastic pipes and furniture maker Asko Oy's components division.

The acquisition "will positively affect our result after financial items," Lehtonen told Reuters by telephone. He was referring to 1997 compared to last year. "It will improve, too," he said, when asked about earnings per share in light of the share issues.

Santasalo-JOT said it would finance the 240 million markka acquisition by issuing 400,000 shares to Asko and by arranging another share issue of 600,000 shares, the terms of which would be announced later.
On Monday, Santasalo released its 1996 report, which showed a 37.9 million markka profit after financial items, up from 25.3 million in 1995. Group EPS was 3.75 markka, up from 3.12.

The acquisition of Asko's cast component units would further improve Santasalo's earnings prospects compared to the outlook given with the 1996 report, which had said that 1997 profits "should rise on the previous year", Lehtonen said.
"Only a fraction of the synergy benefits will be seen this year, but the deal will further improve our earnings prospects for 1998 and 1999," Lehtonen said.
